# Agent Workspace Architecture

> A redacted reference for building agent workspaces: the roles, routines, hooks, memory, and task coordination that turn a coding agent into a system you can hand work to. One person's working setup, published with the reasoning attached.

## Full text

- [llms-full.txt](https://jimy-r.github.io/agent-workspace-architecture/llms-full.txt): The six core documents (README, PATTERNS, META_ARCHITECTURE, EVALUATION, ADOPTION, WORKFLOW) inlined in reading order; the tour, changelog, and samples are linked only. Read this instead of following the links if you want the core reference in one request. Start here.

## Source documents

- [Tour](https://jimy-r.github.io/agent-workspace-architecture/): The interactive tour — layers, modules, patterns, and a task walkthrough. An HTML page: for the same material in markdown, read PATTERNS.md below.
- [The workspace, mapped](https://jimy-r.github.io/agent-workspace-architecture/workspace-map.html): The entire architecture on one page — entry points, the session, the governance floor, persistent state, gated outputs, and the watcher layer. An HTML page built around an inline SVG diagram, so it degrades badly in text extraction: for the same material in markdown, read META_ARCHITECTURE.md below.
- [PATTERNS.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/PATTERNS.md): The eighteen load-bearing patterns, each as problem, pattern, why it beats the obvious alternative, and what it costs.
- [META_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/META_ARCHITECTURE.md): The full structural map of the workspace: layers, modules, personas, routines, hooks, MCP servers, memory, and the task layer.
- [EVALUATION.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/EVALUATION.md): How to tell whether a workspace change actually helped. A golden set of frozen cases replayed K times, deterministic checks rather than an LLM judge, and the five-class fixture discipline that validates a check.
- [ADOPTION.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/ADOPTION.md): A five-step build guide, minimum-viable at each step, for standing up your own workspace.
- [WORKFLOW.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/WORKFLOW.md): How work actually moves through the workspace, session to session.
- [README.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/README.md): Project overview, what the repo is, and how to navigate it.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/AGENTS.md): Runtime-neutral instructions for an agent working in the repo: reading order, the redaction rule, the checks to run, and the commit conventions.

## Learn track

- [learn/README.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/README.md): The guided track index: seven modules over the eighteen patterns, organised by capability, with a time estimate and prerequisite per module.
- [M0. Foundations](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/00-foundations.md): The session loop (orient, plan, work, wrap), run once end to end.
- [M1. Canonical knowledge](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/01-canonical-knowledge.md): One source of truth per fact, with pointers from everywhere else. Patterns 1, 5, 17.
- [M2. Context economics](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/02-context-economics.md): Context as spend: the always-loaded surface, and why position multiplies the price of a read. Patterns 9, 18.
- [M3. Verification & oversight](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/03-verification-oversight.md): Trust through checks: golden cases, audit canaries, and gating a scaffold behind a measurable hypothesis. Patterns 8, 10, 11, 13.
- [M4. Safety & permissions](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/04-safety-permissions.md): Cheap mechanical guards: hooks, tiering by impact, and keeping credentials out of files. Patterns 4, 6, 7.
- [M5. Telemetry & cost](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/05-telemetry-cost.md): Loud failure and priced lanes: the dead-man's switch, and instrumenting a lane before migrating it. Patterns 3, 15.
- [M6. Provenance & delegation](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/learn/06-provenance-delegation.md): Claims that carry sources, work that carries a mandate. Patterns 2, 12, 14, 16.

## Teardowns

- [teardowns/README.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/teardowns/README.md): The teardown index, ground rules, and page conventions. Published architectures read against the eighteen patterns.
- [GPT-RAG](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/teardowns/2026-09-06-azure-gpt-rag.md): Microsoft's Foundry solution accelerator, read at `76a8a4d6fd88`. Decision records that carry an expiry date and falsifiers; the absences cluster on execution — ~300 KB of tests no workflow runs.
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/teardowns/2026-09-05-deepseek-harness.md): DeepSeek's plugin-everything agent runtime, read at `d347e703908d`. Strong on one-home-per-fact and guards proven to fail; no first-party memory, by recorded decision.
- [herdr](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/teardowns/2026-08-28-herdr.md): The Rust runtime that owns the terminals coding agents live in, read at `7b675f42af35`. Pane state and agent-native coordination are ahead of the field; spend, freshness, and provenance are unaccounted.
- [LifeOS](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/teardowns/2026-08-28-lifeos.md): A personal AI operating layer shipped as one self-contained skill, read at `ce046f26495c`. Distribution discipline is exemplary; measurement, silent-failure detection, and provenance are absent.
- [12-Factor Agents](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/teardowns/2026-08-27-12-factor-agents.md): HumanLayer's principles for production LLM applications, read at `d20c728`. The strongest statement of the application layer; the operational layer around it is out of scope by design.

## Optional

- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): Recent activity, dated, newest first. Useful for what changed lately, not for understanding the architecture.
- [samples/](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/tree/main/samples): The full scaffold library — roles, skills, subagents, scheduled tasks, hooks, and Python helpers to fork.
- [samples/board/README.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/samples/board/README.md): The task board module design — card schema, the three rules that carry it, the explicit delegation queue, and why it replaced the retired scheduled project-manager agent.
- [samples/board/board.example.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/samples/board/board.example.md): A synthetic card store in the real field format: ten cards across four areas, a recurring lane, and a queued card.
- [samples/board/agent-queue.SKILL.example.md](https://github.com/jimy-r/agent-workspace-architecture/blob/main/samples/board/agent-queue.SKILL.example.md): The delegation skill — the intake interview run at delegation time, the on-demand drain procedure, and its Iron Laws.
